title: iPhone Duo’s FaceTime camera is JUST for FaceTime..
brief: The hidden inner camera on Apple’s foldable phone is designed mainly for video calls, not high-quality selfies. The story explains why under-display cameras lose image quality: the lens has to photograph through part of the screen, which blocks and scatters light. Apple’s solution is to keep a separate outer camera for normal use, creating a practical tradeoff between an uninterrupted display and better photos.

topic_candidates.title: These ponds help FEED half the people on Earth
topic_candidates.query: Utah blue evaporation ponds potash solution mining fertilizer Utah Geological Survey
topic_candidates.brief: The electric-blue ponds near Moab are not natural lakes: they are solar evaporation ponds used to extract potash, a potassium-rich fertilizer ingredient. The video follows the process from pumping water deep underground, dissolving buried salts, bringing the brine back up and using sunlight to evaporate the water until potash crystals remain. The viewer also gets the surprising reason the ponds change color.
topic_candidates.evidence_summary: The Utah Geological Survey describes the site as a solution mine: water is injected into potash-bearing rock, brine is pumped into evaporation ponds, and potash precipitates as the water evaporates. It also explains that the blue color comes from dye added to improve sunlight absorption and evaporation. USGS identifies potash as an essential crop nutrient used with nitrogen and phosphorus. ([geology.utah.gov](https://geology.utah.gov/map-pub/survey-notes/glad-you-asked/glad-you-asked-what-are-those-blue-ponds-near-moab/?utm_source=openai))

topic_candidates.brief: A viral flexible-lens demo raises a bigger question: can glasses change shape or prescription without bulky mechanics? The video explains how a soft lens can use a flexible membrane and liquid or pressure to alter its optical shape.
